title: Improving Continuous-Rotation Tomography of Cellular Specimens
content: Cryo electron tomography (cryo-ET) has developed into a powerful technique for visualizing the near-native ultrastructure of cells and tissues [1]. The demand for structural information within its native biological context is driving the rapid growth of cryo-ET. However, cryo-ET often requires large data sets, due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of cellular specimens and to the radiation-damage-limited signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of individual tomograms. Since each dataset typically requires tens of minutes to acquire, there is an urgent need to develop faster acquisition schemes to maximize throughput and enable larger-scale experiments. Continuous-rotation acquisition, similar to the method of acquisition in micro-crystal electron diffraction (microED), has the potential to dramatically boost throughput while also potentially improving data quality [2, 3]. However, early attempts at continuous-rotation tomography have shown limited reconstruction quality compared to conventional tilt-series acquisition [3]. Here, we have used an ultra-fast electron counting camera to acquire continuous-rotation cellular tomography data of cortical neurons. Using this system, we have developed and investigated a range of acquisition and processing techniques to improve reconstruction quality to match or exceed that of conventional tomography.
